sourcedFrom: BLASER F16 — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document (UNKNOWN — not printed in the document)
cleanIntro: The F16 Sporting is a break-action over-under with a SELF-COCKING double lock: opening the gun cocks both locks, and after one shot one lock is still cocked. ⚠ It is the one F16 variant this book names outright, and it names it to give it a step of its own: §5.8 is the Sporting's ADJUSTABLE TRIGGER, which slides fore and aft to suit the hand. ⛔ The two sentences that matter most here are not about cleaning at all — Blaser warns that a strong knock or a drop can fire the gun EVEN WITH THE SAFETY APPLIED, and it forbids storing the gun with the muzzle covered.

steps.title: ⛔ Read the barrel first — this book is for the F16 LINE
steps.action: Blaser's own opening instruction is to confirm you have the right book: the model designation F16 and the calibre are marked on the LEFT-HAND side of the barrel. ⚠ That mark names the line, so the general procedure below is the F16's; anything Blaser prints under a variant's own name belongs only to that variant.
steps.prose: The gun tells you which book it takes. Read it before you read the book.
steps.aside: The F16 shotgun is fitted with a self-cocking double lock. When the firearm is opened, two locks are cocked. After one shot is fired, one lock remains cocked.
steps.quote: First of all, check to see that you have the correct operating instructions. The model designation, F16, and the calibre are indicated on the lefthand side of the barrel.
steps.cite: BLASER F16 — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — Introduction

steps.title: ⛔ The safety catch is NOT a drop-safety
steps.action: Apply the safety — slide it to the REAR with your thumb until S is visible — but do not treat it as proof of anything. Blaser states plainly that strong vibration or a drop can fire the gun even with the safety applied. ⛔ Unload; do not merely secure.
steps.prose: A maker who writes this about his own safety is telling you where the real safety is: an open, empty gun.
steps.aside: Ensure that the muzzle always points in a direction in which no person or object is endangered. Only place your finger on the trigger if you are about to fire the firearm.
steps.quote: If the firearm is subjected to strong vibration or dropped, it is possible that shots will be fired even with the safety catch applied.
steps.cite: BLASER F16 — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — 2.3. Applying the safety catch

steps.title: Open it — the ejectors decide what happens next
steps.action: Press and hold the locking lever, tilt the barrel assembly fully down, and watch what the extractors do. Both barrels have an extractor WITH an ejector function, and the ejector is only active on a barrel that has been FIRED. ⚠ So a fired case is thrown clear while a live round is merely lifted — pull the unfired cartridges out by hand.
steps.prose: Two different behaviours from the same part, and which one you get tells you whether that barrel has been fired.
steps.aside: The firearm is cocked when it is opened. Ensure that the muzzle always points in a direction in which no person or object is endangered.
steps.quote: The firearm has an extractor with ejector function on both barrels. After firing a shot, the ejector function for the respective barrel is active. When the firearm is opened, the extractor lifts up the unfired cartridges slightly or ejects the fired cartridges.
steps.cite: BLASER F16 — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — 3.2. Unloading the firearm

steps.title: ⛔ Make it safe and unload BEFORE anything comes apart
steps.action: Blaser's dismantling section opens with a DANGER block and one instruction: make the firearm safe and unload it before dismantling. This is a gun whose locks are cocked by the act of opening it, so an unverified chamber and a cocked lock arrive together.
steps.prose: The gun cocks itself when you open it. That is exactly why this line comes first.
steps.quote: Before dismantling the firearm, make it safe and unload it.
steps.cite: BLASER F16 — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — 1. Assembly, dismantling — DANGER

steps.title: Forearm catch, then the forearm
steps.action: Press the forearm catch and take the forearm off. It comes away from the radius on the action; there is no screw and nothing to lever. ⛔ The barrel assembly cannot come off until the forearm has.
steps.prose: One catch, one part. If it resists, it is still latched.
steps.aside: Mounting the barrel set is only possible when the forearm is removed.
steps.cite: BLASER F16 — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — 1.3. Remove the forearm

steps.title: Unhook the barrels at about 45°, not fully open
steps.action: Press and hold the locking lever and tilt the barrel assembly to roughly 45 DEGREES — not to the fully open position — then pull the hinge pins on the action out of their bearings on the barrel. ⚠ The angle is the whole trick: the pins only line up with their bearings part-way through the swing.
steps.prose: Fully open is the loading position. Forty-five degrees is the takedown position, and they are not the same place.
steps.aside: To quickly become able to handle your firearm safely, have all assembly steps performed by a specialist (e.g. specialist dealer).
steps.cite: BLASER F16 — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — 1.4. Unhook the barrel assembly

steps.title: ⛔ That is the whole strip — three parts, and Blaser stops there
steps.action: Forearm, barrel assembly, action-and-stock. Blaser publishes no further dismantling of the F16 for the owner, and its warranty excludes firearms maintained by third parties. ⛔ Anything past this point is not in the book and is not in this guide.
steps.prose: A three-part gun is a gift. Clean it as three parts.
steps.quote: Blaser Jagdwaffen GmbH recommends that the firearm is maintained and checked after every 10,000 shots and/or every 2 years.
steps.cite: BLASER F16 — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — 6. Care and maintenance

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Steel shot and the tight chokes — a barrel-damage prohibition
deepSteps.action: With steel, tungsten, tungsten/iron or molyshot, Blaser forbids the 3/4 (IM), 1/1 (F) and 5/4 (EF) chokes outright, AND forbids shooting with no choke installed at all. ⚠ The gun does carry a steel shot proofmark — the restriction is about which choke, not about whether.
deepSteps.prose: Steel does not swage down the way lead does. A full choke is where that stops being a theory.
deepSteps.aside: The F16 shotgun has a steel shot proofmark and is suitable for steel shot.
deepSteps.quote: Damage to the barrels due to incorrect or missing interchangeable chokes! When using steel shot, or tungsten, tungsten/iron or molyshot, do not use interchangeable chokes sized 3/4 (IM), 1/1 (F) or 5/4 (EF). Only shoot with the interchangeable chokes installed.
deepSteps.cite: BLASER F16 — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — 5.2. Steel shot cartridges

deepSteps.title: Changing a choke is a safe-and-unload operation, with one tool
deepSteps.action: Blaser wants the gun made safe, unloaded and OPEN before a choke is touched, the thread clean and lightly oiled, and the choke wrench — not pliers, not fingers — used to turn it.
deepSteps.prose: A cross-threaded choke in a barrel is a gunsmith's job that started as a thirty-second one.
deepSteps.quote: Before changing the choke, make the firearm safe and unload it. Only change the interchangeable chokes with the firearm open.
deepSteps.cite: BLASER F16 — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — 5.4. Changing the interchangeable chokes
deepSteps.warn: Damage to the interchangeable chokes by incorrect handling! Ensure that the thread of the interchangeable choke is clean and lightly oiled. Only use the choke wrench to change the choke.

deepSteps.title: ⛔ No oil into the trigger and lock system — it can HARDEN
deepSteps.action: Blaser's warning is mechanical, not fussy: oil and grease that get into the trigger and lock system can resinify — harden — and cause hazardous malfunctions. ⚠ The action's hinge axes DO want grease. The lockwork does not.
deepSteps.prose: Two adjacent parts of the same gun, opposite instructions. Getting them the wrong way round is the classic over-oiled shotgun.
deepSteps.aside: Regularly lubricate the hinge axes and the radius on the action with gun grease.
deepSteps.quote: When cleaning hunting firearms, make sure that no oil or greases ingress into the trigger and lock system. Under certain conditions, oil and greases can resinify (harden) and, thus, cause hazardous malfunctions.
deepSteps.cite: BLASER F16 — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — 6. Care and maintenance — ATTENTION

deepSteps.title: ⚠ Stock oil and gun oil are not interchangeable
deepSteps.action: Blaser says it twice, in opposite directions: stock oil is NOT suitable for the metal parts, and gun oil is NOT suitable for the wood. Its wooden stocks are oil-rubbed and want stock oil.
deepSteps.prose: Two bottles on the bench and it matters which one you reach for.
deepSteps.aside: All wooden stocks from Blaser Jagdwaffen are oil-rubbed. We recommend treating them regularly with Blaser stock oil. Gun oil is not suitable for care of the wood!
deepSteps.quote: All metal parts of the firearm and the interchangeable chokes should be cleaned and lightly oiled. Whenever the chokes are changed, clean the thread with a brass brush. Stock oil is not suitable for care of the metal parts!
deepSteps.cite: BLASER F16 — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — 6. Care and maintenance — metal parts

deepSteps.title: Uncocking the locks — SNAP CAPS, not a bare trigger
deepSteps.action: This gun cocks both locks when it opens, so it can go into the cabinet cocked. Blaser's method for letting them down is snap caps: unload first, muzzle down, snap caps in the chambers, close, check the lever with your index finger, then operate the trigger twice.
deepSteps.prose: Dry-firing a self-cocking lock on an empty chamber is how firing pins end.
deepSteps.quote: Use snap caps to uncock the locks.
deepSteps.cite: BLASER F16 — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — 5.1. Uncocking the locks
deepSteps.warn: Never store the firearm with the muzzle covered or with a muzzle guard attached! Always observe the instructions and warning notices of the care product’s manufacturer!

deepSteps.title: ⚠ Which barrel fires first — the selector, and the handedness
deepSteps.action: A selector lever in front of the trigger picks the first barrel: pushed left to the “U” side the bottom barrel fires first, pushed right to “O” the top one does. ⚠ Blaser also states this design is for right-handed shooters, its locking lever opening to the right.
deepSteps.prose: Worth knowing before a functional check, so you are not surprised by which lock lets down first.
deepSteps.aside: The F16 shotgun is for right-handed shooters. The locking lever in this design opens to the right (right-handed shooters).
deepSteps.quote: To select the barrel for the first or second shot, there is a selector lever in front of the trigger.
deepSteps.cite: BLASER F16 — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — 4.1. Barrel selection and firing

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The Sporting's trigger SLIDES — and only on an unloaded, open gun
deepSteps.action: §5.8 is this variant's own section. The F16 Sporting's trigger can be moved to the rear or to the front for hand size or preference: loosen the trigger holding screw A with a 1.5 mm Allen key, slide the trigger, tighten it again. ⛔ Blaser's DANGER block bounds it — the adjustment is done only with the firearm UNLOADED AND OPEN.
deepSteps.prose: An adjustment inside the trigger guard is exactly the operation where an unverified chamber becomes an injury.
deepSteps.quote: Depending on the size of the hands, or the shooter’s preferences, the F16 Sporting’s trigger can be adjusted to the rear or to the front.
deepSteps.cite: BLASER F16 — OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG — UNKNOWN — no revision code is printed in the document — 5.8. Trigger adjustment F16 Sporting
deepSteps.warn: The trigger adjustment can only be done with an unloaded and open firearm.

cleaning.name: BARREL AND CHOKES
tasks: Bore cleaned; chamber wiped dry and lightly oiled
Choke thread cleaned with a BRASS brush at every choke change
⛔ Never stored with the muzzle covered or a muzzle guard fitted

cleaning.name: ACTION
tasks: Hinge axes and the radius on the action greased with GUN GREASE
⛔ No oil or grease into the trigger and lock system — it can resinify
Locking lever checked closed before the gun is put away

cleaning.name: METAL AND STOCK
tasks: Metal parts cleaned and lightly oiled — ⛔ NOT with stock oil
Wooden stocks treated with stock oil — ⛔ NOT with gun oil
Interchangeable chokes cleaned and their threads lightly oiled

reassembly: Press the locking lever until it engages; push both extractors in to the stop.
Barrel assembly on: hinge pins into their bearings with the barrels angled down.
Fold the rear stock up and check by hand that the locking lever is closed.
Forearm onto the radius on the action, folded up until it snaps into place.
Safety catch applied — S visible — before the gun leaves the bench.
fncheck: With the gun confirmed unloaded, close it and check with your INDEX FINGER that the locking lever has gone home — Blaser asks for a physical check, not a look. Work the safety both ways and confirm the S appears and disappears. Move the barrel selector to U and to O and feel each detent. ⛔ Then remember what Blaser says about its own safety catch: a hard knock can fire this gun with the safety applied, so it goes into the cabinet open and empty, never merely secured.
